title: Identity-open proper coincidence as a strict tower and exchange identification
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. All schemes and morphisms are separated of finite type over $k$. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum], the compactifications $c=(j,p_c)$ of [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and $F_f^c=Rp_{c*}j_!$ with its specified integral realization [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Integral coefficients mean the completed ring sheaf $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site; $D^b_c(T,R)$ is the derived-complete category whose constructible finite reductions have cohomology in one interval independent of $n$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. 

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper and $c_0=(1_X,f)$ its identity-open compactification. Write $a_X:(1_X)_!\xrightarrow{\sim}1$ for the degreewise identity-open identification and $\alpha_{f,n}=Rf_{*,n}(a_X)$ for the finite proper identification [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence]. Let $X'\to X$, $Y'\to Y$ form a Cartesian square with vertical maps $f,f'$ and horizontal maps $g',g$, respectively. Use the finite exchange formula [def-exchange-projection].

For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ with compatible finite-reduction etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], put $K_n=K\otimes_R^LA_n$. Use the strict-system comparison of [lem-sf-compact-support-proper-image-tower] at $j=1_X$ and the completed-exchange realization of [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-strict-tower-realization]. The degreewise $a_X$ identifies the actual strict quotient-transition system defining $F_f^{c_0}K$ with the ordinary direct-image system whose $n$-th term is $\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{*,n}K_n$ and whose $(n+1,n)$ transition is $Rf_{*,n+1}$ of the quotient map $K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}K_n$, followed by the canonical direct-image/coefficient-restriction comparison and restriction to $\widehat R_Y$. This isomorphism commutes with all transitions and projections. Its total derived limit, followed by the specified ordinary-direct-image reconstruction, is the canonical $\alpha_f^R:Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K$; in particular its projection to level $n$ is the finite $\alpha_{f,n}$ after the specified source and target projections.

Use the completed compact-support exchange of [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]. Under $\alpha_f^R,\alpha_{f'}^R$ the integral exchange is exactly the specified completed proper-base-change mate: the open comparison at $1_X,1_{X'}$ is the identity under $a_X,a_{X'}$, including the strict source/target transition identifications. For any other compactification the finite and integral refinement comparisons identify its proper coincidence with the identity-open one, independently of the comparison choices. No comparison between discrete non-torsion etale coefficients is asserted.

proof.text: At $c_0$ the finite comparison is precisely $Rf_{*,n}(a_X)$ by cor-cbc-proper-coincidence. Apply the open-tensor normalization on the ringed diagram site to $j=1_X$. Extension by zero and restriction along this open leave each section unchanged; hence their unit and the open-tensor comparison become identities under $a_X$. This is a sectionwise natural identification of complexes of strict systems, including the quotient arrows, and thus descends to their derived categories. For the finite exchange formula, the same normalization gives $\beta=1$ under $a_X,a_{X'}$: its restriction is the identity and restriction along the identity open is the identity functor. Substituting $p=f$, $j=1_X$ in the two-factor formula leaves exactly the unit--square--counit proper mate, naturally in $K_n$.

source.place: Clause (3), proper coincidence; identity-open finite normalization

proof.text: Apply lem-sf-compact-support-proper-image-tower at $j=1_X$. This open is quasi-compact and $K$ is complete. Its whole-system comparison identifies the compact-support quotient system with the proper-image quotient system for $L=(1_X)_!K$. Conjugate by the sectionwise $a_X$ of step 1. The open reduction comparison is then the identity, so the resulting map $A_\bullet$ has component $A_n=\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,n}(a_X)=\operatorname{Res}_n\alpha_{f,n}$. Explicitly, the compact-support coefficient-restriction comparison is open scalar restriction followed by direct-image scalar restriction. At the identity open its first factor is the identity. Naturality of $a_X$ for the quotient arrow therefore gives $A_n t^!_n=t^*_n A_{n+1}$, with $t^*_n$ exactly direct image of $K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}K_n$ followed by the direct-image restriction comparison. This proves the asserted transition formula on the actual strict quotient diagram, not by testing equality of derived maps at each level.

source.place: Clause (3), original step 16: actual quotient-transition identification

proof.text: Use $\mathcal L=R\lim$ on strict towers. The ordinary reconstruction $b_f:Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L N_\bullet$ is the specified direct-image/limit comparison after the completion unit of $K$. The direct-image-limits theorem supplies this comparison, its quotient projections, and the diagram-site projection normalization. Its adic hypotheses hold: $R$ is a DVR with finite residue field, hence Noetherian, and the finite perfect quotients are supplied by the standard-quotients lemma. Set $\alpha_f^R=b_f^{-1}\mathcal L(A_\bullet)$. The compactification realization $d_{c_0}:Rf_*(1_X)_!K\to Rf_!^{c_0}K$ uses these very completion, open-tensor and direct-image/limit maps. At the identity open its open-tensor factor is the identity by step 1. Thus $\alpha_f^R d_{c_0}=Rf_*(a_X)$, which fixes the canonical proper coincidence rather than choosing a new isomorphism. If $\pi^!_n,\pi^*_n$ denote the two specified tower projections, functoriality of total limit gives $\pi^*_n b_f\alpha_f^R=A_n\pi^!_n$. This is the required finite projection equation. The same argument defines $\alpha_{f'}^R$ on the pulled-back input.

source.place: Clause (3), original step 16: derived limit and its projection normalization; Stacks 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim)

proof.text:
For the completed exchange apply the strict-tower realization at $c_0$. Its hypotheses hold: $K$ is complete with the supplied compatible bounded-below etale-origin witnesses, and $(1_X)_!K$ is just $K$ under $a_X$, with its strict quotient identification from step 1. Pullback supplies the witnessed finite target inputs in the Cartesian square. The realization expresses the completed compact-support exchange as the image of $e^{c_0}=(R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}\beta)E_f^{\mathcal T}$, with exactly its specified source and target reconstruction maps. The tower-open normalization says that identity opens give identity $\beta$ before evaluation. Consequently, after the strict identifications of step 2, $e^{c_0}=E_f^{\mathcal T}$, the normalized proper mate. The completed-exchange definition uses this same proper factor and ordered limit comparisons. Applying the total-limit functor and the reconstructions of step 3 therefore gives
$$\alpha_{f'}^R\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp},c_0}_!=\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_*\,Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}(\alpha_f^R).$$
Here the equality follows by cancelling the identical source/target comparison isomorphisms in the ordered formulas; it is an equality of the specified maps, not a consequence of their finite evaluations.

source.place: Clause (3), original step 17: completed proper exchange with identity open

proof.text: For any other compactification $c$, choose a common refinement with $c_0$, using cofilteredness. Since $X$ is of finite type over $k$, it is Noetherian, so every open immersion out of $X$ (or out of its base change $X'$, of finite type over $Y'$) is quasi-compact; the compactifications are therefore objects of the cofiltered category. At a finite level the compactification-coherence theorem supplies its canonical comparison $I_{c,c_0}$, independent of this choice, with identity and composition cocycles. Define proper coincidence for $c$ by $\alpha_{f,n}I_{c,c_0}$. The cocycle says that composing any further refinement comparison gives this same map. The witnessed domain required here is precisely the supplied etale-origin domain for each $K_n$. Thus this construction identifies finite proper coincidence for all comparison choices; it does not extend the finite coherence theorem to arbitrary unwitnessed pro-etale complexes.

Work in constant $R$-coefficient strict-tower coordinates. The CBC refinement-exchange theorem gives actual isomorphisms $I_{c,c_0}$ with $I'_{c,c_0}e^c=e^{c_0}G_gI_{c,c_0}$, independently of common refinement and arrows. It applies with $B=R$, $\Lambda_n=A_n$ and the supplied bounded-below witnesses to $M=\mathcal R(UK)$: the constant-completion equivalence gives $\operatorname{ev}_n\mathcal R(UK)=UK\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline{A_n}\cong K\otimes^L_{\widehat R}A_n=K_n\cong\nu^*L_n$, compatibly with the quotient transitions. It imposes no common Tor interval. The compactified-word realization identifies the completed-ring compactification words and their strict comparisons with these coordinates, including their quotient transitions and augmentations, without a uniform Tor bound. Its single-word normalization is the specified compactification realization. Applying $\mathcal L$ to the displayed equation and conjugating by those realization maps gives maps between $U(Rf_!^cK)$ and $U(Rf_!^{c_0}K)$ and their exchange equation. Both objects are derived complete, and restriction of scalars $U$ is an equivalence from derived-complete $\widehat R$-modules to derived-complete constant $R$-modules by the constant-completion equivalence; hence these maps and equations are the images under $U$ of unique integral maps $I^R_{c,c_0}$ and equations in $D(\widehat R_Y)$, $D(\widehat R_{Y'})$. The intermediate realization and its inverse cancel in a composite of two comparisons, so the cocycle and independence remain equalities of integral maps. Define $\alpha_f^{R,c}=\alpha_f^{R,c_0}I^{R}_{c,c_0}$; the cocycle identifies every refinement-defined proper coincidence with it. Combining this equation with step 4 proves the asserted integral exchange identification for every compactification. Only completed coefficient sheaves and their finite reductions were used.
